findings.claim: Category-order validation drops all other rules with repeated category or direction fields while checking a rule's alternatives. This suppresses a category-order fault that occurs when supplied values on different rules coexist.
findings.repro: In a minimal v2 table with the standard bank-code rule and no category_order, add two credit name rules. Give rule A direction: in and repeat category with cash_deposit and revenue_transfer. Give rule B category: revenue_card_settlement and repeat direction with in and out. With A's cash_deposit and B's in as their sole values, validation reports that the trading-receipts bucket lacks a category order. With the repeats present, the validator checks A without B and B without A, so it reports the repeats but omits that ordering fault.

findings.claim: The mandatory bank-code check reads a repeated pattern through its placeholder and reports the bank-code rule missing even when every supplied pattern has the required text.
findings.repro: In the shipped v2 table, duplicate the returned_dd rule's exact pattern field, preserving `'^UNPAID DD\b'` as both values and leaving bank_code: true. Either value alone satisfies the check. Together they trigger the correct duplicate-pattern refusal plus the incorrect claim that no rule carries the required bank code.

findings.claim: Bank-code shape checks can report an invalid flag and forbidden anchor solely because the other repeated fields remain placeholders.
findings.repro: In the shipped v2 returned_dd rule, repeat direction with any and in, and repeat stage with line_type twice. Every selection preserves an allowed anchored bank-code rule. The flag check at line 502 sees at least one placeholder on every variant and reports an invalid bank-code shape. The anchor check also sees the direction placeholder and reports a forbidden anchor.

findings.claim: The README claims a matching profile name can settle an ambiguous credit and omits cheque wording from its description of payment-method conflicts.
findings.repro: Classify a positive FPS CASH DEPOSIT JANE DOE with Jane Doe as a profile director. src/cma/categorise.py:1292–1302 keeps it unexplained and adds profile:director to the candidates. Classify a positive CHEQUE CASH DEPOSIT and the cheque is also recorded as a candidate in an ambiguous verdict.
